anti_overlap: Do NOT audit the recall-gate 'exercised' predicate's ledger/reconciliation logic as a self-consistency question -- that is the bookkeeping reviewer's charge; you only care about whether a PRODUCED box actually COVERS real pixels.
Do NOT reason about the out-of-scope person_silenced_face justification's honesty or the substrate/off-manifold argument as an accounting claim; stay on the physical coverage-bond of boxes.

Leave the trickery of marking a genuine miss as 'exercised' via double-entry-style compensating errors to the ledger reviewer; your version of that concern is narrowly the physical map/clamp/dilate transform producing a non-covering box.
decision_lens: For every place the design claims coverage is added or unioned, ask: does this box actually adhere to the real face pixels after mapping/clamping/dilation, or does it merely EXIST in the list? And can any later stage lift, crowd out, or dedup away a coat that a real face depended on?
distance_rationale: A pre-modern East Asian craft with centuries of refinement, structurally unrelated to software or ML. Its core discipline is layered redundant coverage where each successive coat must actually bond to the substrate beneath it and cure into the whole; a repair that merely LOOKS continuous (a bridged gap, a hollow seam, a coat that skinned over without bonding) fails silently under use. This is isomorphic to a redaction system that stacks two independent coverage paths (person-crop face + independent full-frame face) and claims their UNION is always safe -- but only if each path genuinely covers where it appears to, boxes genuinely bond to the pixels of the face, and 'over-coverage is the safe direction' actually holds under mapping/clamping/dilation. No AI-cliche domain overlap.
expected_isomorphisms: Layered coats that must each bond to substrate <-> two coverage paths whose UNION is only safe if each box actually covers the face pixels it claims (letterbox mapping, clamp, dilation preserve coverage, not merely produce a box somewhere)

A hollow/bridged seam that looks continuous but is unbonded <-> a face `cls` box that exists in the detection list but, after map_box_from_letterbox / _clamp_box / dilate_box, does NOT actually overlap the real face region (coverage-mask gap the gate can't see because a box was produced)

'One more coat never hurts' craft rule vs a coat that traps moisture and lifts the whole repair <-> the diff's 'over-coverage is always the safe direction, no NMS needed' claim -- is there ANY path where an extra/misplaced union box shifts, replaces, or crowds out a real one (dedup, tracker association, downstream selection) rather than purely adding?

Curing order and interaction between coats <-> ordering of step 2 (person-crop) vs step 2b (full-frame) vs step 3 (plate) appending into one `detections` list; whether either face path can be shadowed, filtered, or NMS'd against the other downstream despite the 'no dedup' claim

A coat applied where the eye expects coverage but the surface was contaminated (no adhesion) <-> the full-frame pass emitting a face box that satisfies the gate's 'face_boxes is non-empty' exercised test while the actual ground-truth region stays uncovered
focus: Whether the union-coverage safety claim is actually true end-to-end: that a produced face box genuinely covers the real face pixels after all coordinate transforms, that stacking paths only ever adds coverage, and that no downstream stage can silently subtract one path's coverage.
name: fd-urushi-lacquer-repair-coverage-bond
persona: Apply the perspective of a master urushi lacquer-repair artisan who has spent decades learning that a repair is only as sound as the bond of its weakest coat -- that a seam which merely LOOKS whole to the eye, but did not truly adhere to the surface beneath, is more dangerous than an obvious crack because it invites confident use of a vessel that will fail. This reviewer distrusts any claim that 'more coverage is always safe' without tracing whether each added layer actually bonds to the thing it is meant to protect, and whether layers can interfere with one another during curing.
review_areas: The map_box_from_letterbox -> _clamp_box -> _is_degenerate -> dilate_box chain on the full-frame face box: any input (extreme aspect ratio, box near frame edge, tiny box) where the emitted `face` detection lands OFF the real face region yet still counts as a produced face box for the exercised predicate

The 'no NMS-style dedup needed because coverage only unions' claim: trace every downstream consumer of `cls==face` boxes (tracker, timeline, redact layer, and any dedup/NMS the diff does NOT touch) for a path where two overlapping face boxes get merged/suppressed and the SURVIVOR covers less than the union

vision_face_conf_x100 as a SEPARATE knob defaulting equal to face_conf_x100: whether a future/misconfigured raise of this threshold silently removes the entire independent coat while the crop path is ALSO missing -- the exact double-miss the union was supposed to prevent

Ordering and mutation of the shared `detections` list across steps 2, 2b, 3 -- whether step 2b appending after step 2 can be reordered, filtered, or truncated anywhere such that the full-frame coat is dropped preferentially

The dilation-off test asserts an EXACT box equal to the pure mapping; verify the production path (dilation on, default 10%) still yields coverage that includes the ground-truth face and that dilation direction cannot shrink coverage at a clamped edge
Whether 'a face is redacted if EITHER path finds it' survives the case where BOTH paths produce a box but a shared downstream dedup keeps only one and that one is the smaller/misplaced box
severity_examples: P0: a downstream NMS/dedup stage (not shown in the diff but consuming cls==face) suppresses the full-frame face box in favor of an overlapping-but-smaller crop box, so the union claim is false and a real face edge ships unredacted while the gate stays green.

P1: for a face box near the frame edge, _clamp_box + dilation produce a box that no longer overlaps the ground-truth region, yet face_boxes is non-empty, so the recall gate marks the fixture EXERCISED and PASSING while coverage is actually missing.

P2: vision_face_conf_x100 defaulting equal to face_conf_x100 gives a false sense of an independent safety net; one config edit raising it disables the entire decoupling with no gate signal, because the crop path alone still marks face fixtures exercised.
source_domain: Japanese urushi lacquerware repair (kintsugi / negoro multi-coat build-up)
success_hints: Read cascade.py's actual dilate_box, _clamp_box, _is_degenerate, and map_box_from_letterbox implementations, not just the diff hunk -- the bond failure lives in the transform math, not the append

Grep the whole jawnscope-node tree for any NMS or dedup or IoU-based suppression that runs on detections AFTER run_cascade returns; the diff's 'no dedup needed' claim is only true if no such stage exists anywhere downstream

Distinguish 'a face box was produced' from 'the ground-truth face pixels are covered' -- the gate's coverage mask is the real test; the exercised predicate is a weaker proxy the produced-box could satisfy without real coverage

Trace conf_x100=0 vs raw.conf_x100: the crop head-fallback uses score 0 while the full-frame pass carries a real score -- check whether any downstream 'keep highest-confidence box' logic would then prefer a real-score box and drop a score-0 backstop
task_context: Find any path where this independent full-frame face pass lets a face go unredacted, silently disables the person->crop path, or lets the recall gate go green while a real face is uncovered. Verify the exercised-predicate decoupling can't be tricked into marking a genuine miss as 'exercised'. Rank by §8.5 redaction-recall risk, not style. Apply the layered-bond discipline: for every claimed unit of added coverage, verify the box actually adheres to the real face pixels after all coordinate transforms, and that no downstream stage can lift, crowd out, or dedup away a coat a real face depended on.
